text: All microscopy was performed post DTA as sections through the melted (and subsequently distorted) cylinders while still in the alumina sample cups. The same standard procedures for extracting drilled chemistry samples was followed as in S. Imhoff et al. (2020) with the exception that a 1/4” diameter bit was used. To summarize, chip samples are extracted without coolant and a very low spindle speed to prevent bit erosion or oxidation of the samples. The ICP-MS and ICP-OES digestions follow very similar procedures which differ only in final dilution factor. Chemistry samples are taken from buttons on both the top and bottom surfaces (the arc and hearth facing sides respectively after the final melt). These are averaged except if noted. ICP-OES measures the U and Mo content independent of trace elements, essentially solving for x in Equation 7. The trace elements (C, N, ...) are determined by ICP-MS and LECO combustion analysis to determine y. About 0.5 grams of each sample was weighed out and placed in Savillex vessels. 10 mL of the acid mixture was added 26 Figure 12: Schematics describing material preparation, various samples being taken (drill and EDM), the sample position error, and volumes being sampled. to each vessel. The vessels were closed and set to react on a hot plate for 4-6 hours. Each vessel was checked for completion. The vessel containing the U −16 wt.%Mo sample still had undigested metal in it after the time was up, so 0.2 ml of HF was added to help the remaining material digest. After all samples were digested, the contents of each vessel were poured into a 50 ml falcon tube, rinsed out with DI water 3 times, and then each falcon tube was brought up with 1% HNO3 to reach 50 ml. Prep blanks and duplicates of select samples were also made to check for contamination/quality control. 200X dilutions were taken from each initial dilution to prepare samples for analysis. For ICP-OES analysis, 0.05 mL of each initial dilution was added it to a 10 ml falcon brought up with 1% HNO3 . Three custom-made multi-element standard solutions produced by Inorganic Ventures were used in the calibration of these samples. Two different lot numbers of the standards were used for calibration and verification. Standard solutions were prepared differently for each machine. For ICP-OES, a much higher calibration range was used since uranium and molybdenum content are the focus for this instrument. For ICP-OES the target range was from 1 ppm to 100 ppm.
